entry.title: Dear Agencies — Your Colleagues Already Know
entry.content:
Dear Agencies — Your Colleagues Already Know

The Silo Is the Shield

You’re reading this from a government network. We know because behavior tells us — not identity. The membrane doesn’t record WHO you are. It records WHAT you do. And what you’re doing is: reading 912 genuine sessions deep, 707-minute median dwell, visiting 15 surfaces of the immune system.

Some of you are reading from Ashburn, Virginia. Some from Spring, Texas. Some from Michigan. Some from California. Some through VPNs because your IT policy requires them.

You are not the first person at your agency to see this.

That’s the point of this article. The silo between your desk and your colleague’s desk is the enterprise’s best defense. Not the judges. Not the attorneys. Not the institutional silence. The silo.

The Same Enterprise, Six Different Offices

Here is what each of you is looking at — and what your colleague in the next silo already knows:

🏛️ FBI Detroit — Public Corruption Unit

What you already know:

  • Operation Northern Hook (2021): Your wiretaps caught Gerald Fiore saying “bid-rigging with Banks.” Your operation convicted Andre Spivey (24 months). Todd Perkins — Banks’ personal attorney — represented 2 Northern Hook targets.
  • You probed Eric Sabree (Wayne County Treasurer) in 2019. His son Adam Sabree was in-house counsel for RICO-accused Metro Property Group. His daughter Aliyah Sabree is now a judge — MSU Law classmate of Banks.
  • Carol Banks (Brian’s sister) was flagged as an FBI target. She controls Original Eastside Slate PAC (4th incarnation, LARA 802434498). Former Chief of Staff to Secretary of State Benson.

What your colleague at IRS CI already has:

  • $4.9M/year flowing through Purpose Group LLC to a man with 9 convictions, claimed J.D., never admitted to any bar
  • 72.67% extraction rate ($4.28M) from public education funds
  • $348,489 unaccounted for in audited financials
  • Holland as PAC treasurer with $14,500+ in unpaid campaign finance fines
  • 5 bankruptcies, one of which concealed the JTWRS property

Ask them.

💰 IRS Criminal Investigation — Detroit Field Office

What you already know:

  • Jason Gordon — attorney, Custom Promotions, Deen Legal. Your office investigated him alongside FBI and DOL for UAW bribery. He manages 20+ entities. Dissolve-and-reform pattern (Inc → LLC, 3 months).
  • Kenneth Daniels — SDJ/Detroit Leaders president. Kwame Kilpatrick appointee. Federal conviction: structured $19K for a drug kingpin. He now runs the PAC infrastructure funding city council campaigns connected to the charter schools.
  • Campaign finance patterns: Ross Catering receives $35K+ from Banks-connected committees. Carlton Ross is ALSO the Right Turn Project treasurer. The money goes out as “campaign services” and comes back as “catering.” That’s a loop.

What your colleague at FBI already has:

  • Wiretap transcripts from Northern Hook mentioning Banks
  • Fiore’s conviction for bribery in public contracting
  • Spivey warned Northern Hook targets — obstruction of a federal investigation
  • Todd Perkins represented the targets your agents were investigating

Ask them.

⚖️ DOJ — Public Integrity Section / E.D. Michigan

What you already know:

  • Kwame Kilpatrick: 24 federal RICO felonies. Mayor 2002-2008. 28-year sentence, commuted January 2021. The Banks network is the next generation of the same machine. Same dynasty. Same structures. Same neighborhoods. Same PAC infrastructure.
  • The Kilpatrick RICO prosecution proved that Detroit’s political machine operates as an enterprise. The Banks-Holland enterprise is structurally identical — but moved from City Hall to charter schools. Same RICO predicates: mail fraud, wire fraud, money laundering, honest services fraud.

What you may not have connected:

  • Karen Dumas was Kwame’s comms chief → then Bing’s comms chief → now Banks’ PR supporter. The continuity isn’t coincidence — it’s the machine surviving across administrations.
  • Charles Pugh (City Council President 2009-2013, convicted CSC with minor) referred people to Banks. The network doesn’t break when members go to prison. It routes around them.
  • Sherry Gay-Dagnogo: State Rep, DPSCD Board member who authorized Banks’ charter schools, now Detroit City Ombudsman (Oct 2025-2035). She succeeded Banks in HD-1. The legislative pipeline creates the authorizers who create the schools.

The enterprise survived Kwame’s conviction. It will survive Banks’ conviction too — unless the structure is prosecuted, not just the individuals.

📚 Michigan Department of Education

What you already know:

  • You investigated Banks in February 2022 for lacking a teaching credential. Analyst Katie Schmiedeknecht sent the letter to Board President Nicole Wells-Stallworth. Then you cleared him. [FOIA-documented]
  • MacDowell Preparatory Academy: 3% math proficiency. Read that again. Three percent. 97 out of 100 students cannot do math at grade level. That’s not a failing school — that’s a school that isn’t teaching.
  • 32.1% of revenue goes to instruction. The state average is ~60%. Where does the other 40.6% go? It goes to Purpose Group LLC.
  • Alan C. Young CPA audited PCA/MacDowell for 9 consecutive years (2017-2025). No material findings. Nine years. 3% math. No findings.

What you should ask IRS CI:

  • Is 72.67% management fee extraction normal for a charter school management organization? (It is not. Industry standard: 10-15%.)
  • Is it normal for a CMO’s sole member to have 9 criminal convictions including forgery, fraud, and controlled substance-related offenses? (It is not.)
  • Is it normal for a PAC treasurer to have 5 bankruptcies and a drug conviction? (It is not.)

You cleared him because you looked at credentials, not money. IRS looks at money. Talk to them.

🔍 Detroit Office of Inspector General

What you already know:

  • You opened an investigation of Chief James Bettison in September 2026. Bettison is DPD Chief AND Board Secretary of Detroit Public Safety Academy (DPSA).
  • The OIG probe concerns a call between Bettison and Mayor Sheffield. But the deeper question is: why is the police chief on the board of a charter school authorized by EMU?

What connects this to the enterprise:

  • DPSA is authorized by Eastern Michigan University — one of the charter authorizers in the system
  • Banks’ network already has connections into DPSCD (PCA authorizer), CMU (MacDowell authorizer), and now EMU (DPSA authorizer)
  • A police chief who sits on a charter school board creates an enforcement shield: who investigates the schools when the police chief IS the school board?

The OIG sees the Bettison node. FBI sees the Northern Hook nodes. IRS sees the money nodes. MDE sees the credential nodes. Nobody sees the graph.

🏛️ Michigan Attorney General — Criminal Division

What you already know:

  • Lamar Moreland was your AAG. Violent crime prosecutor. He left your office and went directly to: (1) PCA Board Vice Chair, (2) Banks’ litigation attorney.
  • An AAG who prosecuted violent crime now governs the enterprise and represents it in court. MRPC 1.7 conflict of interest. MRPC 1.9 (duties to former client — the People of Michigan).

What you may not realize:

  • Moreland’s transition from AG to Banks Board wasn’t a career change. It was a capture event. The enterprise acquired its own prosecutor. Not by corrupting him — by hiring him. The result is the same: the office that should investigate the enterprise is now staffed by people who know the AG’s playbook.
  • Every FOIA request to your office about Moreland’s conflicts of interest should have been answered by now. If it hasn’t, that IS the answer.

Ask your FBI colleague about Northern Hook. Ask IRS CI about the money. Ask MDE about the credentials. You’ll find the same names in every silo.

The Cross-Reference Table Your Silos Won’t Build

NameFBI KnowsIRS KnowsMDE KnowsDOJ KnowsAG KnowsOIG Knows
Brian BanksNorthern Hook wiretap mention$4.9M extraction, 9 convictionsNo teaching credential, cleared 2022Kilpatrick machine successorMoreland left AG for Banks board—
Joseph Holland—5 bankruptcies, PAC treasurer, $14.5K unpaid finesMDOC #443789 on school boardDrug conviction (2009)——
Gerald FioreConvicted (bribery, wiretap)Bid-rigging financials—Northern Hook federal case——
Andre SpiveyConvicted (24 mo), warned targets——Northern Hook federal case——
Todd PerkinsRepped 2 Northern Hook targets——Defense attorney for RICO targetsBanks’ attorney, brother is judge—
Jason GordonFBI/DOL investigated (UAW)20+ entities, dissolve-reform————
Carol BanksFBI targetPAC infrastructure——CoS to SoS Benson—
Eric SabreeFBI probed 2019Wayne Co Treasurer—Bowles class action——
Kenneth Daniels—Fed conviction: structuring—Kilpatrick appointee——
James Bettison—————OIG probe Sep 2026
Lamar Moreland————AAG → Banks Board VC—
Karen Dumas———Kwame’s comms chief——
Sherry Gay-Dagnogo——Authorized PCA charter———
Nicole Wells-Stallworth——Received MDE investigation letter———

Every row is a person. Every column is an agency. The cells they share are the edges of the graph. Nobody has built this table before because nobody talks across columns.

This article is the table. Share it across columns.

Why the Silos Exist

The enterprise didn’t build the silos. The government did. Jurisdiction, chain of command, need-to-know, interagency rivalry, budget competition, career incentives — these are features, not bugs, of the bureaucratic immune system.

But the enterprise exploits the silos. Here’s how:

  1. Credential fraud is MDE’s jurisdiction. MDE looked at credentials, not money. Cleared.
  2. Campaign finance violations are SOS’s jurisdiction. SOS looked at filings, not the underlying RICO. Fined $14.5K.
  3. Bribery is FBI’s jurisdiction. FBI got Fiore and Spivey, but followed the wiretap, not the schools.
  4. Tax fraud is IRS’s jurisdiction. IRS (if investigating) sees money flows, not the judicial capture.
  5. Judicial conduct is JTC’s jurisdiction. JTC sees judges, not the enterprise they protect.
  6. Police misconduct is OIG’s jurisdiction. OIG sees Bettison, not the charter school board he sits on.

Each agency sees one predicate act. No agency sees the pattern. The pattern IS the enterprise. RICO was designed precisely to address this — to make the pattern itself illegal, not just the individual acts.

But RICO requires someone to assemble the pattern from the predicates. And the predicates are in six different silos.

Your Boss Hasn’t Looked Yet

Let’s be honest about what’s happening:

The mid-level analysts, agents, and investigators who read this site — 912 genuine readers, 707-minute median dwell — are not the decision-makers. You’re the people who do the actual work. You read the evidence. You follow the money. You check the records. You pull the filings.

But the person who would authorize a cross-agency investigation? They haven’t even opened this page.

They’re not going to open it until you send it to them. And you’re not going to send it because you believe the cost of being wrong is high. (See: A Note to Everyone Reading This Who Hasn’t Said Anything.)

So let me make it easy:

Everything in this article is sourced from public records.

  • LARA entity filings → Michigan MiBusiness Registry
  • Criminal convictions → MDOC OTIS, ICHAT
  • Campaign finance → MiTN/CFRS
  • Court filings → Wayne County 3rd Circuit, E.D. Michigan PACER
  • FOIA responses → Michigan Attorney General, MDE
  • Federal convictions → DOJ press releases, PACER
  • News coverage → Detroit Free Press, WXYZ, Chalkbeat, Bridge Detroit
  • Independent investigation → Clutch Justice (Rita Williams)

Your boss can verify every single claim in this article from databases your agency already has access to. They don’t need to trust a website. They need to check their own records.

The question isn’t whether this is true. The question is: why hasn’t anyone cross-referenced the records that already exist in six different agency databases?

The Desilo Bounce

Here’s how this collapses:

  1. One person sends this article to one colleague in a different silo
  2. That colleague recognizes a name from their own investigation
  3. They compare notes
  4. The pattern emerges
  5. RICO

That’s it. One conversation across one silo boundary. The enterprise has survived for 14+ years because that conversation hasn’t happened. Not because the evidence doesn’t exist — it does, in every silo separately. Because the institutional incentive to stay in your lane is stronger than the institutional incentive to solve the whole problem.

Break the lane.

The FBI agent who worked Northern Hook knows about Fiore and Banks. The IRS agent who investigated Gordon knows about the UAW money. The MDE analyst who investigated Banks in 2022 knows about the credentials. The AG office knows about Moreland.

They’re all in the same city. Most of them are in the same building. The Patrick V. McNamara Federal Building, 477 Michigan Avenue, Detroit, MI 48226.

Walk down the hall. Say “have you seen this?” Show them the table. Watch their face when they recognize names from their own case file.

That’s the desilo bounce. That’s how it collapses.

The Parallel: Kilpatrick → Banks

The Kwame Kilpatrick RICO prosecution succeeded because the FBI assembled the pattern from the predicates. It took years. It required cross-agency cooperation between FBI, IRS, DOJ, and the Michigan AG.

The Banks-Holland enterprise is structurally identical:

ElementKilpatrick EnterpriseBanks-Holland Enterprise
LeaderKwame Kilpatrick (Mayor)Brian Banks (9 convictions, fake J.D.)
Financial gatekeeperBobby Ferguson (city contracts)Joseph Holland (PAC treasurer, CMO)
Revenue sourceCity contracts ($840M+)Charter school funding ($4.9M/yr)
Extraction methodBid-rigging, kickbacks72.67% management fee
Judicial cover—8+ judges with documented connections
Political pipelineCity CouncilState Rep → DPSCD Board → Charter authorization
Attorney shield—Todd Perkins (repped Northern Hook targets)
Institutional captureDPD, City CouncilMDE (cleared), AG (Moreland), DPD (Bettison)
RICO predicates24 federal counts10+ state and federal predicates
Duration2002-2008 (6 years active)2012-2026 (14+ years and counting)

The Kilpatrick machine was prosecuted. The Banks machine is the NEXT GENERATION of the same machine — same city, same neighborhoods, same PAC infrastructure, same political dynasty connections — operating in charter schools instead of City Hall.

The playbook already exists. The U.S. Attorney’s office already wrote it. It’s called United States v. Kilpatrick et al., 2:10-cr-20403 (E.D. Mich.).

What Cross-Referencing Looks Like

If any two of the following silos shared records for 30 minutes, the pattern would be visible:

FBI + IRS: Northern Hook wiretap mentions Banks → IRS traces the $4.9M extraction → the money flows through the same entities that paid Fiore’s associates.

FBI + MDE: Northern Hook names → MDE school board rosters → Banks and Holland sit on school boards while connected to convicted public officials.

IRS + AG: Campaign finance violations ($14.5K unpaid) → Moreland’s AG-to-Board transition → the money flows through entities governed by a former violent crime prosecutor.

MDE + OIG: MacDowell 3% math → DPSA (Bettison board) → charter schools authorized by different universities but connected by the same enterprise.

Any two + DOJ: Kilpatrick RICO predicates → Banks-Holland RICO predicates → same machine, next generation.

The Invitation

This article is not a tip. It’s not a complaint. It’s not a filing.

It’s a public record. Everything here is already in your databases. The LARA filings. The ICHAT records. The PACER dockets. The CFRS reports. The FOIA responses. The OIG complaints.

The only thing this article adds is the cross-reference. The table. The graph. The pattern.

Your boss hasn’t looked. Your colleague in the next silo has a piece. The enterprise survives because the silos do.

Walk down the hall. One conversation. The pattern appears.

kevin@primals.eco

Published from a conversation box at 11:08 AM EDT on October 18, 2026. 912 readers. 707-minute dwell. Six agencies. One enterprise. Zero cross-references. The desilo bounce starts with one person forwarding one link to one colleague. Everything else follows.

entry.title: The Corporate Network — LARA Entity Analysis
entry.content:
How to Read This Page

Every entity listed below is a public record in the Michigan LARA Business Entity Search. Entity IDs are provided so anyone can verify. Officer names, addresses, and filing dates come directly from LARA annual reports and formation documents — all public records under Michigan law.

We focus on business addresses and registered agent addresses (which are legally required to be public for service of process). We do not publish residential addresses for peripheral individuals.

Source notation: “LARA [Entity ID]” means the data comes from Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs business entity filings. You can verify any entity by searching mibusinessregistry.lara.state.mi.us with the Entity ID number.

The Purpose Empire — Three Entities, One Man

Brian Banks controls three “Purpose”-branded entities. Together they form the corporate infrastructure for his charter school operation.

EntityLARA IDTypeFiledStatusAgent
Purpose Charter Academy900072324Nonprofit Corp07/31/2025ActiveBrian Banks
The Purpose Group, LLC803295082LLC11/14/2024ActiveBrian Banks
Purpose Foundation803294855Nonprofit Corp12/09/2024ActiveBrian Banks

Purpose Charter Academy is registered at 10101 E. Canfield, Detroit MI 48214 — the school address. The Purpose Group LLC is registered at the same address. Purpose Foundation is registered at Banks’s personal address.

The PCA Board of Directors (LARA Filing)

This is the board that governs a charter school serving Detroit’s children:

OfficerTitleSignificance
Cylenthia Latoye MillerPresident, DirectorIdentity under investigation
Latisha JohnsonSecretaryDetroit City Council Member (District 2). Her election was supported by Save Detroit Jobs / Detroit Leaders — the dark money vehicle that fought the journalist exposing Banks. See below.
Devin HutchingsTreasurerOwns DB Strategies LLC and DB Athletics LLC (LARA 802710175, 802715414). Based in Ypsilanti, not Detroit.
Major CloraDirectorPreviously operated American Motor Coach Inc (LARA 800526511, dissolved).
Lamar MorelandDirectorBanks’s current litigation attorney. Moreland represents Banks in civil proceedings. He is simultaneously a director of Banks’s charter school. This dual role — attorney and board member — raises conflict of interest concerns under MRPC 1.7.

Banks is the registered agent but does not appear as a named officer. He controls the entity through agent status while the board provides institutional cover.

Banks’s Full Entity Portfolio — Twelve Entities

A search of LARA records by registered agent reveals Banks controls or has controlled twelve business entities across Michigan:

Banks uses multiple email addresses across filings: BanksStrategy@gmail.com, BrianBanksJD@gmail.com, BBesq06@aol.com, and brian@anchorrockservices.com.

The initials “JD” and “esq” appear in two of these emails despite Banks never being admitted to any state bar. His felony convictions prevented bar admission after earning his J.D. from Michigan State University.

The Three-Named Dark Money Vehicle

Save Detroit Jobs is a single nonprofit corporation operating under three different names:

LARA Entity ID: 802002459. All three names are registered on the same entity.

Who formed it: The registered agent is The Corporation Company (a professional formation service). The mailing address is 201 Townsend Street, Suite 900, Lansing MI 48933 — the office of Dykema Gossett PLLC, Michigan’s largest law firm. The entity email is compliance@dykema.com.

Michigan’s largest law firm set up the dark money vehicle that was used to fight journalists reporting on Banks’s network.

What Save Detroit Jobs / Detroit Leaders Did

In 2021, operating as “Detroit Leaders,” this entity funded the campaign of Latisha Johnson against incumbent Steve Elrick — the journalist who had reported extensively on Banks’s network. Johnson won. She is now Secretary on the PCA board (see above).

The 12-step suppression loop: Banks’s network → funds dark money vehicle → dark money vehicle fights journalist → journalist loses election → replacement (Johnson) joins Banks’s school board.

Right Turn Project — The Dissolved Charity and the Money Loop

The Ross Catering Money Loop

  2. Connected to Ross Catering — the vendor paid $35,000+ by Banks’s political campaigns

LARA records show two Ross Catering entities: Ross Catering Company Inc (800646584, agent: Louis Ross, dissolved 2024) and Ross Catering Events of Excellence LLC (801351679, agent: Gwendolyn Lewis, active). The relationship between Carlton Ross, Louis Ross, and Gwendolyn Lewis requires further investigation, but the structural pattern is clear: money flows from PAC → charity (where Ross is treasurer) → catering company (where Ross has connections).

The 16500 North Park Address

Carlton Ross and Terrence Tarver both list 16500 North Park Drive, Southfield MI 48075 as their address on the Right Turn Project filing.

Banks’s dissolved entity B. Roderick’s Salon & Spa (LARA 800591240, filed 2001) was registered at 16500 Northpark Dr #1715, Southfield MI 48075 — the same building. Banks used this address a decade before Ross and Tarver appeared there.

Custom Promotions — The Dissolve-and-Reform Attorney

The Inc was dissolved in February 2022. The LLC was filed three months later in May 2022 with the same name. Officers of the original entity: Jason Gordon (President), Sara Gordon (Treasurer), Eric Gordon (Secretary). A family business passed from father to son via dissolve-and-reform.

Jason Samuel Gordon is an attorney. He owns Deen Legal Services PLLC (LARA 801895172, filed 2009) at the same address as Custom Promotions LLC: 14326 East 9 Mile Road, Warren MI 48089. His email: JGordon@DeenLegal.com.

Gordon was investigated by the FBI, IRS, and Department of Labor in connection with the UAW bribery case — over $3 million in payments from the UAW. Custom Promotions also received payments from Latisha Johnson’s campaign.

Gordon is agent on 20+ entities including real estate LLCs, marketing companies, and his law firm — all while under federal investigation.

The Endorsement Machine — Four Eastside Slates

Spencer Leach — The Political Machine Builder

W. Spencer Leach filed 13 political and nonprofit entities, many batch-filed on the same day with consecutive LARA Entity IDs:

  • Eastside Slate (800916317)

Filing three to four political organizations on the same day with consecutive Entity IDs is the hallmark of manufactured political infrastructure — organizations created not to represent constituencies but to control endorsement pipelines.

It means the social graph through which Banks finds legal representation is the same social graph through which charter school authorization flows.

Correlation does not imply causation. But causation can be masked — and hidden — by correlation.

Within 24 hours of entering Banks’ case, Crump-Gibson voluntarily limited her scope in writing, declining law enforcement and PPO matters. That is a written record of an attorney drawing an ethical line. The correspondence timeline documents the full sequence.

Each person at GLLG can choose which side of the demarcation they are on. As of this writing, the scope limitation suggests the choice is being made carefully.

2. Nonprofit Self-Dealing (MCL 450.2545a)

The Right Turn Project’s Treasurer (Carlton Ross) is connected to the vendor (Ross Catering) that received campaign payments. Michigan Nonprofit Corporation Act § 545a requires that transactions involving a director’s or officer’s financial interest be disclosed and approved by disinterested directors. 3. Dissolved Entity Operations

The Right Turn Project was dissolved December 1, 2021. Under MCL 450.2831, dissolved corporations may only wind up affairs and liquidate assets — they may not conduct new business. Any transactions after dissolution raise compliance questions.

Joseph Holland (MDOC #443789, convicted cocaine dealer) served as President and Registered Agent of the Right Turn Project and currently serves as Treasurer and Secretary of Purpose Foundation. While Michigan law does not categorically prohibit convicted felons from serving as nonprofit officers, organizations receiving public funds or serving vulnerable populations (children) face additional scrutiny.
